resources.title: Program Security
resources.description: This is the second path offered by Pwn.College covering Program Security, Reverse Engineering, Retun Oriented Programming, Dynamic Allocator Misuse, and Program Exploitation.

resources.title: System Security

resources.title: Web cache deception
resources.description: This learning path covers web cache deception vulnerabilities. Youll learn how to identify discrepancies between how the origin server and cache handle requests and how to leverage the discrepancies to create path confusion.

resources.title: WebSockets vulnerabilities
resources.description: This learning path covers the identification and exploitation of security vulnerabilities specific to WebSockets in web applications.

resources.title: Authentication vulnerabilities
resources.description: This learning path explores authentication vulnerabilities, which have a critical impact on security. Youll learn about common mechanisms and vulnerabilities, and strategies for robust authentication.

resources.title: Server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks
resources.description: This learning path teaches you about server-side request forgery (SSRF). Youll learn about its impact, common techniques used in attacks, and how to defend against them.

resources.title: Prototype pollution
resources.description: This learning path introduces you to prototype pollution vulnerabilities in JavaScript. Youll learn what prototype pollution is, how it can be exploited, and how to prevent it in your applications.

resources.title: Clickjacking (UI redressing)
resources.description: This learning path deals with clickjacking attacks. Youll learn the fundamentals of clickjacking, how to construct basic attacks, and implement server-side and client-side defense strategies.

resources.title: GraphQL API vulnerabilities
resources.description: This learning path explores common vulnerabilities associated with GraphQL APIs due to implementation and design flaws. Youll learn how to find GraphQL endpoints, bypass some common defenses, and exploit a range of GraphQL API vulnerabilities.

resources.title: Cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)
resources.description: This learning path provides an in-depth understanding of CORS, including common examples of CORS-based attacks and how to protect against these attacks.

resources.title: Path traversal
resources.description: This learning path covers path traversal vulnerabilities. Youll learn how to carry out path traversal attacks and circumvent common obstacles. Youll also learn how to prevent path traversal attacks.

resources.title: NoSQL injection
resources.description: This learning path covers the detection, exploitation, and prevention of NoSQL injection vulnerabilities. Youll explore the differences between NoSQL and SQL injection, learn how to perform NoSQL syntax injection, and how to use NoSQL operators to manipulate queries.

resources.title: Race conditions
resources.description: This learning path covers race conditions, a common vulnerability in web applications where concurrent processes lead to unintended behavior. Youll learn how to identify, exploit, and prevent race conditions, leveraging tools like Burp Suites Repeater and the Turbo Intruder extension.

resources.title: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
resources.description: This learning path covers CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery). Youll learn about some common CSRF vulnerabilities, and how to prevent them.

resources.title: File upload vulnerabilities
resources.description: In this learning path, youll explore how simple file upload functions can become a vector for severe attacks. Youll learn how to bypass common defense mechanisms to upload a web shell, enabling full control over a vulnerable web server.

resources.title: Web LLM attacks
resources.description: This learning path teaches you how to perform attacks using Large Language Models (LLMs). Youll learn how to construct attacks that take advantage of an LLMs access to data, API, and user information that you would not be able to access directly.

resources.title: API testing
resources.description: This learning path teaches you how to test APIs that arent fully used by the website front-end. Youll learn key API recon skills to help you discover more attack surface. In addition, youll learn how to identify server-side parameter pollution vulnerabilities that may impact internal APIs.

resources.title: Server-side vulnerabilities
resources.description: This learning path introduces you to a range of common server-side vulnerabilities. This is perfect if youre new to web security and want to get an overview of the kinds of vulnerabilities that exist, as well as how an attacker might identify and exploit them in real-world systems.

resources.title: SQL injection
resources.description: This learning path introduces SQL injection (SQLi), a critical web vulnerability. Youll learn how to detect and exploit SQLi to uncover hidden data and manipulate application behavior, as well as essential techniques to secure applications against SQLi attacks.

resources.title: OST
resources.description: Dedicated Space for learning all sorts of topics with a focus on low-level exploitation.

resources.title: Android Forensics & Security Testing
resources.description: This class serves as a foundation for mobile digital forensics, forensics of Android operating systems, and penetration testing of Android applications. Although delivered in a single offering, the course can be broken into separate offerings.

resources.title: Flow Analysis & Network Hunting
resources.description: This course focuses on network analysis and hunting of malicious activity from a security operations center perspective. Netflow strengths, operational limitations, tools, visualization, analytic tradecraft and hunting scenarios.

resources.title: Hacking Techniques and Intrusion Detection
resources.description: This course covers the most common methods used in computer and network hacking with the intention of learning how to better protect systems from such intrusions. Reconnaissance, system scanning, network and application level attacks, and denial of service.

resources.title: Introductory Intel x86: Architecture, Assembly, Applications, & Alliteration
resources.description: This course teaches the basic concepts and describes the hardware that assembly code deals with. It also goes over many of the most common assembly instructions. Students will be shown it is possible to read most programs by knowing only around 20-30 instructions and their variations.

resources.title: Introduction to ARM
resources.description: This class builds on the Intro to x86 class and tries to provide parallels and differences between the two processor architectures wherever possible while focusing on the ARM instruction set, some of the ARM processor features, and how software works and runs on the ARM processor.

resources.title: An Introduction to Cellular Security
resources.description: This course is intended to demonstrate the core concepts of cellular network security. Although the course discusses GSM, UMTS, and LTE - it is heavily focused on LTE. The course first introduces important cellular concepts and then follows the evolution of GSM to LTE.

resources.title: Introduction to Network Forensics
resources.description: This is a mainly lecture based class giving an introduction to common network monitoring and forensic techniques. This class is meant to be accompanied by lab exercises to demonstrate certain tools and technologies, but the lab exercises are not absolutely necessary to convey the operating concepts.

resources.title: Introduction to Secure Coding
resources.description: The purpose of this course is to provide developers with a short, focused primer related to secure coding. The hope is that each developer will leave the course with a better understanding of how they can improve, from a security perspective, the code that they write.

resources.title: Introduction to Vulnerability Assessment
resources.description: This is a lecture and lab based class giving an introduction to vulnerability assessment of some common computing technologies. Instructor-led lab exercises are used to demonstrate specific tools and technologies.

resources.title: Introduction to Trusted Computing
resources.description: This course is an introduction to the fundamental technologies behind Trusted Computing. You will learn what Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) are and what capabilities they can provide both at an in-depth technical level and in an enterprise context.

resources.title: Offensive, Defensive, and Forensic Techniques for Determining Web User Identity
resources.description: This course looks at web users from a few different perspectives. First, we look at identifying techniques to determine web user identities from a server perspective. Second, we will look at obfuscating techniques from a user whom seeks to be anonymous. Finally, we look at forensic techniques.

resources.title: Pcap Analysis & Network Hunting
resources.description: Introduction to Packet Capture (PCAP) explains the fundamentals of how, where, and why to capture network traffic and what to do with it. Covers open-source tools like tcpdump, Wireshark, and ChopShop.

resources.title: Malware Dynamic Analysis
resources.description: This introductory malware dynamic analysis class is dedicated to people who are starting to work on malware analysis or who want to know what kinds of artifacts left by malware can be detected via various tools. Persisting, Communicating, and Hiding.

resources.title: Secure Code Review
resources.description: This course is designed to help developers bring a secure coding mindset into typical project peer reviews. The course briefly talks about the development lifecycle and the importance of peer reviews in delivering a quality product.

resources.title: Smart Cards
resources.description: This course shows how smart cards are different compared to other type of cards. It is explained how smart cards can be used to realize confidentiality and integrity of information.

resources.title: The Life of Binaries
resources.description: How binaries live: compilation, linking, loading and execution on modern OSes.

resources.title: Understanding Cryptology: Core Concepts
resources.description: This is an introduction to cryptology with a focus on applied cryptology. It was designed to be accessible to a wide audience, and therefore does not include a rigorous mathematical foundation (this will be covered in later classes).

resources.title: Understanding Cryptology: Cryptanalysis
resources.description: A class for those who want to stop learning about building cryptographic systems and want to attack them. This course is a mixture of lecture designed to introduce students to a variety of code-breaking techniques and python labs to solidify those concepts.

resources.title: Introduction To Software Exploits
resources.description: Software vulnerabilities are flaws in program logic that can be leveraged by an attacker to execute arbitrary code on a target system. This class will cover both the identification of software vulnerabilities and the techniques attackers use to exploit them.

resources.title: Exploits 2: Exploitation in the Windows Environment
resources.description: This course covers the exploitation of stack corruption vulnerabilities in the Windows environment. Windows mitigations DEP, ASLR, SafeSEH, SEHOP and their bypasses. Fuzzing and exploit development for real Windows bugs.

resources.title: Intermediate Intel x86: Architecture, Assembly, Applications, & Alliteration
resources.description: Building upon the Introductory Intel x86 class, this class goes into more depth on topics already learned, and introduces more advanced topics that dive deeper into how Intel-based systems work.

resources.title: Advanced x86: Virtualization with Intel VT-x
resources.description: Hands on introduction to Intel hardware support for virtualization. Deep dive on the Intel virtualization API and labs to begin implementing a blue pill / hyperjacking style demonstration. Virtualization detection techniques.

resources.title: Advanced x86: Introduction to BIOS & SMM
resources.description: Why the BIOS is critical to the security of the platform. Capabilities and opportunities provided to an attacker when BIOSes are not properly secured. Tools for performing vulnerability analysis on firmware, as well as firmware forensics.

resources.title: Introduction To Reverse Engineering Software
resources.description: In this course we will explore what drives people to reverse engineer software and the methodology and tools used to do it.

resources.title: Reverse Engineering Malware
resources.description: This class picks up where the Introduction to Reverse Engineering Software course left off, exploring how static reverse engineering techniques can be used to understand what a piece of malware does and how it can be removed.

resources.title: Rootkits: What they are, and how to find them
resources.description: Rootkits are a class of malware which are dedicated to hiding the attacker's presence on a compromised system. This class will focus on understanding how rootkits work, and what tools can be used to help find them.

resources.title: The Adventures of a Keystroke: An in-depth look into keyloggers on Windows
resources.description: User mode and kernel mode keylogging techniques including the undocumented ones. PS/2 hardware coverage plus discussion of USB keyloggers.

resources.title: OST2
resources.description: Version 2 of OST — the modern OpenSecurityTraining catalog.

resources.title: Architecture 1001: x86-64 Assembly
resources.description: This class serves as a foundation for the follow on 'Architecture 2001: x86-64 OS Internals' class. Teaches the basic concepts and describes the hardware that assembly code deals with plus the most common instructions.

resources.title: Architecture 4031: Introductory coreboot
resources.description: Bootstrapping knowledge about coreboot design principles and boot process. Prepares a coreboot development environment in the way professional coreboot service providers use.

resources.title: Debuggers 2011: Intermediate WinDbg
resources.description: This mini-course teaches you how to use the Windows Debugger (WinDbg) to debug the Windows kernel, for exploration of OS internals, as we do in Architecture 2001: x86-64 OS Internals

resources.title: Architecture 4001: x86-64 Intel Firmware Attack & Defense
resources.description: Background you need to understand how x86-64 reset vector firmware works, and what the most common security misconfigurations are. Read and understand existing attack and defense research in the space.

resources.title: Debuggers 1015: Introductory Simics
resources.description: This course teaches you how to use the Simics full system simulator debugger well enough to use it in classes that depend on it (like Architecture 4001.)

resources.title: Reverse Engineering 3201: Symbolic Analysis
resources.description: Hands-on class using several Python frameworks against CTF challenges: a binary analysis framework called angr and a SMT solver called z3.

resources.title: Reverse Engineering 3011: Reversing C++ Binaries
resources.description: Advanced reverse engineering class for security researchers who want to expand their horizons and skills in reverse engineering C++ binaries. Techniques and tools for dealing with C++ Binaries.

resources.title: Hardware 1101: Intel SPI Analysis
resources.description: Going below the Intel Memory Mapped Input/Output (MMIO) interface, we sniff the actual SPI commands that are issued on the SPI bus by the Intel hardware to the SPI flash chip.

resources.title: Vulnerabilities 1001: C-Family Software Implementation Vulnerabilities
resources.description: Dual-audience class. For developers who want to learn how to write code without introducing new vulnerabilities, and for aspiring code auditors and freelance vulnerability hunters. Prerequisite for eventually learning about exploitation.

resources.title: Vulnerabilities 1002: C-Family Software Implementation Vulnerabilities
resources.description: Continuation of Vulns1001: more subtle memory, integer, and logic bugs, plus the tooling that finds them.

resources.title: Architecture 4021: Introductory UEFI
resources.description: World of UEFI and PI Specifications. Firmware fundamentals, key terminology, and a succinct overview of the history of BIOS implementations. Essential UEFI concepts and how they shape the boot flow on modern platforms.

resources.title: Architecture 2821: Windows Kernel Internals 2
resources.description: Core concepts on the Windows operating system both in user and kernel lands. Core kernel functionality, what you will typically encounter while exploiting kernels, and how to approach targeting any kernel.

resources.title: Debuggers 3011: Advanced WinDbg
resources.description: Configure an advanced Windows kernel debugging environment. Two VMs, a debugger and a target. Automated deployment of executables between them, and decompiled source-level debugging with IDA/Ghidra plus ret-sync.

resources.title: Exploitation 4011: Windows Kernel Exploitation: Race Condition + UAF in KTM
resources.description: CVE-2018-8611 on Windows 10 x64 1809 (RS5): a complex race condition that leads to a use-after-free on the non-paged kernel pool. Deep dive into KTM (tm.sys).

resources.title: Debuggers 3301: HyperDbg
resources.description: Leverage HyperDbg's unique features to conduct in-depth analysis of both kernel and user executions. Operates on top of Windows by virtualizing a running system using Intel VT-x, without relying on APIs and traditional software debugging mechanisms.

resources.title: Debuggers 1012: Introductory GDB
resources.description: This mini-course teaches you how to use the GNU Debugger (gdb) well enough to use it in classes that depend on it (like Architecture 1001: x86-64 assembly or Architecture 1005: RISC-V assembly.)

resources.title: Architecture 1005: RISC-V Assembly
resources.description: Top-down approach of looking at simple C code, compiling it, and then understanding the assembly instructions that were generated. Programatically-randomized games and spaced repetition to reinforce memorization.

resources.title: Secure Development 1001: C-Family Implementation Vulnerabilities 1
resources.description: For developers who want to learn how to write code without introducing new vulnerabilities. Taught from the perspective of teaching developers the same things vulnerability hunters learn when they're getting into that engineering discipline.

resources.title: Secure Development 1002: C-Family Implementation Vulnerabilities 2
resources.description: Follow-up to SecDev1001 covering subtler defects and modern mitigation strategies.

resources.title: Debuggers 1102: Introductory Ghidra
resources.description: Basic introduction to Ghidra, with an emphasis on using Ghidra as a debugger, so that it can be used in OST2 assembly classes' final exercise.

resources.title: Trusted Computing 1101: Introductory Trusted Platform Module (TPM) usage
resources.description: Trusted Platform Modules (TPM) are the most popular hardware security modules (HSM), widely adopted in personal computers, workstations, network equipment and servers.

resources.title: Trusted Computing 1102: Intermediate Trusted Platform Module (TPM) usage
resources.description: Builds upon TC1101 and expands our skillset with usage of TPM-based machine identity, system integrity (attestation) and deep dive into the Endorsement Hierarchy.

resources.title: Debuggers 1101: Introductory IDA
resources.description: This mini-course introduces the IDA user interface and focuses on how to use the debugger. Covers installation, loading a binary, using breakpoints, stepping through execution, and examining memory and registers.

resources.title: Architecture 2001: x86-64 OS Internals
resources.description: How ring 0 vs. ring 3 privilege separation works at a deep level on Intel hardware. Gives you an incredibly strong foundation for Windows, Linux, *BSD, or macOS OS Internals classes.

resources.title: Debuggers 1011: Introductory WinDbg
resources.description: This mini-course teaches you how to use the Windows Debugger (WinDbg) well enough to use it in classes that depend on it (like Architecture 1001: x86-64 assembly.)

resources.title: Fuzzing 1001: Introductory white-box fuzzing with AFL++
resources.description: Introduction to fuzzing: goals, techniques, practical applications in software security testing. Fundamentals, working process, and various categories like mutation-based, generation-based, and coverage-guided fuzzing.

resources.title: Debuggers 1103: Introductory Binary Ninja
resources.description: Introduces the Binary Ninja user interface and focuses on how to use the debugger. Loading a binary, using breakpoints, stepping through execution, and examining memory and registers.

resources.title: TPM 2.0 Programming using Python and the tpm2-pytss libraries
resources.description: Foundational TPM 2.0 concepts and practical hands-on development techniques for interacting with TPM hardware and simulators, using the Python-based tpm2-pytss library.

resources.title: Bluetooth 2222: Bluetooth reconnaissance with Blue2thprinting
resources.description: Bluetooth reconnaissance and device identification using the Blue2thprinting security tool, for security researchers investigating devices in an enterprise or for known-vuln detection.
